claims.claim: Thailand has no wealth tax

sources.name: PwC: Thailand, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 24 August 2026. "There are no net wealth/worth taxes in Thailand." Inheritance tax is paid by the heir, "regardless of nationality", only on the amount above THB 100 million from each testator; "The inheritance tax rate is 10%", 5% for "heirs who are ascendants or descendants of the testator"; legacies to a spouse are exempt. The page does not say where the property must be.

sources.says: Headline net wealth/worth tax rate "NA" ("the territory does not have the indicated tax") for Thailand (last reviewed 24 August 2026), Malaysia (16 June 2026), Vietnam (23 September 2026), Indonesia (11 June 2026) and the Philippines (01 August 2026).

claims.claim: Residents are those present 180+ days in a calendar year

sources.name: PwC: Thailand, residence
sources.says: Last reviewed 24 August 2026. A resident is present for an "aggregate period of 180 days or more in any tax (calendar) year".

sources.name: Thai Law Online: Thailand foreign income remittance tax, what applies in 2026
sources.says: Dated 1 August 2026, "Last updated 10 November 2026". Section 41: a person staying "a period or several periods totalling 180 days or more" in a tax year is resident; "Income earned before 1 January 2024 falls outside the new interpretation" (Por. 162/2566); the same-year exemption "has not been published in the Royal Gazette" (as of 19 October 2026). The page does not address loans or loan proceeds, nor the LTR.

claims.claim: Since 2024, residents pay up to 35% on foreign income arising from 2024 when it is brought into Thailand, so dividends left in the US account are untaxed

claims.claim: LTR holders are exempt on remitted foreign income (Royal Decree 743)

sources.name: BOI: Royal Decree No. 743 (LTR tax exemptions), English translation
sources.says: B.E. 2565 (2022), given 21 May 2022 (text recovered from the PDF's compressed streams). Section 5: income tax "shall be exempted for a foreigner categorised as Wealthy Global Citizen, Wealthy Pensioner, or Work-from-Thailand Professional who is granted a Long-Term Resident Visa" for assessable income "derived in the previous tax year from an employment, or from business carried on abroad, or from a property situated abroad, and brought into Thailand."

claims.note: The decree covers the Wealthy Global Citizen, Wealthy Pensioner and Work-from-Thailand Professional categories (not the Highly Skilled Professional), for income "derived in the previous tax year" and brought in. The profiles' shorter wording stands; the Wealthy Pensioner route they describe is covered.

claims.claim: Inheritance tax is 5% for descendants above THB 100m per heir, paid by the heir

sources.name: PwC: Thailand, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 24 August 2026. "There are no net wealth/worth taxes in Thailand." Inheritance tax is paid by the heir, "regardless of nationality", only on the amount above THB 100 million from each testator; "The inheritance tax rate is 10%", 5% for "heirs who are ascendants or descendants of the testator"; legacies to a spouse are exempt. The page does not say where the property must be.

sources.name: Thai Law Online (French edition): inheritance tax in Thailand
sources.says: "Dernière mise à jour le 2 novembre 2026". The tax is "à la charge de la personne qui reçoit"; liable are Thai nationals, non-Thais "ayant un domicile dans le Royaume conformément à la loi sur l'immigration", and non-Thais who receive "une succession constituée d'un bien situé en Thaïlande"; 5% for ascendants and descendants, 10% otherwise; "Le seuil est par bénéficiaire, par personne décédée" (THB 100 million).

sources.name: PwC: quick chart, inheritance and gift tax rates
sources.says: Thailand (24 August 2026): inheritance 10, gift 5; Malaysia (16 June 2026): NA, NA; Vietnam (23 September 2026): 10, 10; Indonesia (11 June 2026): NA, NA; Philippines (01 August 2026): "There is no inheritance tax in the Philippines." "an estate tax of 6% is imposed on the assets of the decedent taxpayer."

claims.claim: It reaches non-Thai heirs living abroad only on property in Thailand, so US assets left to US-resident children are outside it

sources.name: Thai Law Online (French edition): inheritance tax in Thailand
sources.says: "Dernière mise à jour le 2 novembre 2026". The tax is "à la charge de la personne qui reçoit"; liable are Thai nationals, non-Thais "ayant un domicile dans le Royaume conformément à la loi sur l'immigration", and non-Thais who receive "une succession constituée d'un bien situé en Thaïlande"; 5% for ascendants and descendants, 10% otherwise; "Le seuil est par bénéficiaire, par personne décédée" (THB 100 million).

sources.name: Forvis Mazars: Thailand Inheritance Tax Act
sources.says: Dated 3 September 2015. Liable: Thai nationals; a non-Thai "who has residence in Thailand under the immigration law"; and a non-Thai "who is receiving an inheritance of property situated in Thailand". 10%, "reduced to 5%" for descendants and ascendants, on inheritances "exceeding 100 million baht".

claims.note: Both pages list the three groups liable; a non-Thai heir with residence in Thailand is taxed whatever the property's location, which does not touch the profiles' case of US-resident children. PwC says only "regardless of nationality". localTaxes.ts (TH) agrees.
